questions.text: Can you tell me what you do?
questions.say: Good afternoon. My name is George, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about what you do. Can you tell me what you do?

cueCard.topic: Describe a library you have visited.
cueCard.explain: and explain how you felt about this library.

questions.text: Describe a library you have visited.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a library you have visited. You should say: where it is; when you went there; what you did there; and explain how you felt about this library.

questions.text: Have you been back to this library since then?
questions.say: Thank you. Have you been back to this library since then?

questions.text: Why do some people still prefer to use libraries rather than the internet?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a library you have visited, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all libraries. Why do some people still prefer to use libraries rather than the internet?

questions.text: How have libraries changed in recent years?
questions.say: How have libraries changed in recent years?

questions.text: Do you think libraries will still exist in fifty years?
questions.say: Do you think libraries will still exist in fifty years?

questions.text: Which public services are most important in a town or city?

questions.text: Should public services such as libraries and museums be free?
